prompt: In a cyclohexane ring, when can the anti periplanar requirement for an E2 reaction be met?

choices.text: Only when the hydrogen and the leaving group are trans diaxial
When the hydrogen and the leaving group are both equatorial
choices.why: If either the leaving group or the hydrogen is equatorial, E2 elimination can't occur.

choices.text: When the leaving group is axial and the hydrogen is equatorial
choices.why: Both must be axial. An equatorial hydrogen isn't anti periplanar to an axial leaving group.

choices.text: When the hydrogen and the leaving group are cis on neighboring carbons
choices.why: Cis groups on neighboring carbons can't both be axial. The two must be trans and diaxial.

explanation: Chair geometry forces a rigid relationship between substituents on neighboring carbons. The anti periplanar requirement can be met in cyclohexanes only if the hydrogen and the leaving group are trans diaxial.

prompt: What happens if the leaving group on a cyclohexane ring is equatorial in the conformation the molecule is in?

choices.text: E2 elimination can't occur from that conformation
E2 occurs with a neighboring equatorial hydrogen instead
choices.why: An equatorial leaving group and an equatorial hydrogen aren't anti periplanar, so E2 can't occur.

choices.text: E2 occurs faster, because equatorial groups are less hindered
choices.why: E2 needs the leaving group axial. An equatorial leaving group blocks E2 from that conformation.

choices.text: E2 occurs, but always gives the Zaitsev product
choices.why: No E2 happens from that conformation at all; the leaving group must first become axial.

explanation: If either the leaving group or the hydrogen is equatorial, E2 elimination can't occur. In Figure 11.9.1's example, the chair with Cl axial eliminates HCl, while the chair with Cl equatorial gives no reaction.

prompt: For E2 reactions of cyclohexanes, which requirement takes priority in deciding the product?

choices.text: The anti periplanar requirement, which overrides Zaitsev's rule
Zaitsev's rule, which overrides the anti periplanar requirement
choices.why: It's the other way around: menthyl chloride gives the non-Zaitsev product because only one trans-diaxial hydrogen is available.

choices.text: Markovnikov's rule
choices.why: Markovnikov's rule is about adding HX to alkenes, not about eliminations.

choices.text: Whichever hydrogen is equatorial
choices.why: An equatorial hydrogen can't be anti periplanar to the leaving group, so it can't be removed by E2.

explanation: The anti periplanar requirement for E2 reactions overrides Zaitsev's rule in cyclohexanes. If the only trans-diaxial hydrogen gives the less substituted alkene, that is what forms, as with menthyl chloride.

prompt: Neomenthyl chloride undergoes E2 elimination of HCl on reaction with ethoxide ion how many times faster than menthyl chloride?
explanation: Neomenthyl chloride reacts 200 times faster than menthyl chloride. The simple change in chlorine stereochemistry produces a 200-fold change in rate and a complete change of product.

prompt: What is the major alkene from E2 elimination of HCl from neomenthyl chloride with ethoxide ion?

choices.text: 3-menthene, the more substituted (Zaitsev) product
2-menthene, the less substituted (non-Zaitsev) product
choices.why: 2-Menthene is the product from menthyl chloride, which has only one trans-diaxial hydrogen.

choices.text: An equal mixture of 2-menthene and 3-menthene
choices.why: Neomenthyl chloride gives 3-menthene as the major product, following Zaitsev's rule.

choices.text: No alkene, because its chlorine is axial
choices.why: An axial chlorine is exactly what E2 needs.

explanation: Neomenthyl chloride's more stable chair has the methyl and isopropyl groups equatorial and the chlorine axial, a perfect geometry for E2. Loss of the axial hydrogen on carbon 4 gives the more substituted alkene, 3-menthene, as Zaitsev's rule predicts.

prompt: What alkene does menthyl chloride give by E2 elimination?

choices.text: 2-menthene, a non-Zaitsev product
3-menthene, the Zaitsev product
choices.why: 3-Menthene is neomenthyl chloride's product. In menthyl chloride's reactive chair, the only trans-diaxial hydrogen leads to 2-menthene.

choices.text: A mixture in which 3-menthene predominates
choices.why: Under E2 conditions only one trans-diaxial hydrogen is available, so the product is 2-menthene.

choices.text: No alkene, because its chlorine can never become axial
choices.why: It can, by ring-flipping to a higher-energy chair conformation.

explanation: Menthyl chloride must ring-flip to a higher-energy chair with all three substituents axial. E2 elimination then occurs with loss of the only trans-diaxial hydrogen available, giving the non-Zaitsev product 2-menthene.

prompt: Which describes the more stable chair conformation of neomenthyl chloride?

choices.text: Methyl and isopropyl groups equatorial, chlorine axial
All three substituents equatorial
choices.why: That is the more stable chair of menthyl chloride, which can't undergo E2 in that conformation.

choices.text: All three substituents axial
choices.why: That is menthyl chloride's higher-energy chair, reached by a ring-flip.

choices.text: Chlorine equatorial, methyl and isopropyl axial
choices.why: In neomenthyl chloride the bulky groups are equatorial and the chlorine is axial.

explanation: Neomenthyl chloride has the methyl and isopropyl groups equatorial and the chlorine axial, a perfect geometry for E2 elimination. That's why it reacts directly from its more stable conformation, and 200 times faster than menthyl chloride.

prompt: What must menthyl chloride do before it can undergo E2 elimination?

choices.text: Ring-flip to a higher-energy chair in which all three substituents are axial
Ring-flip to a lower-energy chair in which the chlorine is axial
choices.why: Its more stable chair has all three groups equatorial. The chair with axial chlorine is higher in energy.

choices.text: Lose Cl− to form a carbocation
choices.why: That would be an E1 pathway. E2 occurs in one step from a chair with the chlorine axial.

choices.text: Nothing; its chlorine is already axial in the more stable chair
choices.why: In menthyl chloride's more stable chair, all three substituents, chlorine included, are equatorial.

explanation: Menthyl chloride has a conformation in which all three substituents are equatorial. To achieve the trans-diaxial geometry, it must first ring-flip to a higher-energy chair conformation in which all three substituents are axial.

prompt: Which isomer would you expect to undergo E2 elimination faster, cis- or trans-1-bromo-4-tert-butylcyclohexane?

choices.text: The cis isomer, because its bromine is axial in the more stable chair
The trans isomer, because its bromine is axial in the more stable chair
choices.why: With the bulky tert-butyl group equatorial, the trans isomer's bromine is equatorial too.

choices.text: The trans isomer, because both of its groups are equatorial and it is more stable
choices.why: E2 needs an axial leaving group. With both groups equatorial, the bromine can't be trans diaxial to a hydrogen.

choices.text: Both react at the same rate, because they have the same groups
choices.why: Their conformations differ: only the cis isomer has an axial bromine when tert-butyl is equatorial.

explanation: The tert-butyl group stays equatorial. In the cis isomer that puts the bromine axial, ready for trans-diaxial E2 elimination; in the trans isomer the bromine is equatorial, so E2 can't occur from the stable chair. The cis isomer reacts faster (Exercise 11.9.1).

prompt: In the reactive chair of menthyl chloride, with all three substituents axial, how many hydrogens are trans diaxial to the chlorine and available for E2 elimination?
explanation: E2 elimination from this conformation occurs with loss of the only trans-diaxial hydrogen available, which leads to the non-Zaitsev product 2-menthene.
